name: Kid Dynamite
label: Jade Tree
lede: Dan Yemin and Dave Wagenschutz left Lifetime behind, found a singer who was headed for film school, and fit 38 songs onto two Jade Tree records. The band ended in February 2000, then kept coming back for benefits and festivals until 2013.

eras.title: Out of Lifetime, into Philly
eras.text: When Lifetime fell apart, Yemin and Wagenschutz kept going in Philadelphia. With Shevchuk singing they made something faster and meaner, and Jade Tree had its debut out within six months of the first show.

years.h: Dan Yemin and Dave Wagenschutz start Kid Dynamite in Philadelphia
years.p: Both walk in straight from [[Lifetime|c9329809-8510-45b9-9202-5640398ddaee]]. Steve Ferrell takes the bass.

years.h: A self-released cassette introduces Jason Shevchuk
years.p: The demo is titled Six Songs with Jay Singing, and it is the first time anyone hears the singer.

years.h: Kid Dynamite opens for Better Than a Thousand
years.p: The first show is April 22, 1998, in Philadelphia, on a bill with the band of Youth of Today's Ray Cappo.
years.xp: Shevchuk got the singing job after the band tried out several other vocalists. The demo cassette came out the same year, and the debut album followed that October.

years.h: A summer of East Coast shows before the studio
years.p: The band plays a run of dates up the coast, then books Trax East for September.

years.src: Wikipedia: Kid Dynamite (album) · Wikipedia: Kid Dynamite (band)
years.h: Jade Tree puts out the debut six months after the first show
years.p: Kid Dynamite (JT1039) is recorded in September at Trax East in South River, New Jersey, with [[Steve Evetts|ae091a4c-0a25-4555-8874-5f05768d9d18]], who had produced Lifetime. Several of the 20 songs run under two minutes.
years.xp:
The album runs 27:06. Among the tracks are Pause, Table 19, Bookworm and Wrist Rocket, with a few short instrumental interludes between them.

Wikipedia's album page lists the bassist as Steve Farrell; the band page spells it Ferrell.

eras.title: Shorter, faster, gone
eras.text: Kid Dynamite toured hard, swapped bass players twice and cut a second album in seventeen days. Then Shevchuk left for film school, and the band played its last shows the same month the record came out.

years.h: Two splits: Sub City with 88 Fingers Louie, and one for I Stand Alone
years.p: The Sub City record (SC004) is shared with Chicago's [[88 Fingers Louie|2cf874cd-6bb2-49a3-956a-a7228e7a317f]]. The second is a 7-inch on I Stand Alone Records (ISA #05).

years.h: Steve Ferrell leaves, and Ernie Parada keeps the bass seat warm
years.p: [[Ernie Parada|586bfe03-6a6f-4aa5-bac8-d2f97d2acfb6]] covers temporarily until Michael "Spider" Cotterman takes the job for good.

years.cap: Kid Dynamite at Karma Club, Boston, August 15, 1999
years.h: Kid Dynamite spends the summer opening for Good Riddance
years.p: The tour goes coast to coast, with Boston's [[In My Eyes|f8a4cb28-0443-48af-b58a-b2b2ab51206d]] on the bill.

years.h: Evetts is back for Shorter, Faster, Louder, tracked September 1 to 17
years.p: [[Dave Hause|feb265ec-e510-4277-9451-914e3c6ceac5]] sings backups and Ernie Parada adds vocals as the second album comes together at Trax East.
years.xp: Wikipedia also credits Alison Mennor with vocals on some tracks. Three months after the sessions ended, Shevchuk was gone.

years.h: Late-1999 bills pair the band with Kill Your Idols, Snapcase and Buried Alive
years.p: The shows run alongside [[Kill Your Idols|b6154aed-416f-43bf-93fe-0906b051535f]], [[Snapcase|90f7f8df-db45-4a6c-89fb-9e912f77eabd]] and Buried Alive.

years.h: Shevchuk leaves for film school, and the band calls it
years.p: Jason Shevchuk goes in December 1999 to finish his degree. Kid Dynamite chooses to end rather than find another singer.
years.xp:
Right Brigade's Jesse Standhard was rumored as a replacement. Wikipedia says that never happened.

The band closed with two albums and the same singer on both.

years.h: The last two nights are at First Unitarian Church
years.p: Kid Dynamite plays February 18 and 19, 2000, in the Philadelphia church basement that anchored the city's punk scene.

years.big: "A punk rock marathon, designed for moshing until the audience drops from exhaustion."
years.src: Wikipedia: Shorter, Faster, Louder · Wikipedia: Kid Dynamite (band)
years.h: Shorter, Faster, Louder lands the month the band quits
years.p: That is CMJ New Music Report on a Jade Tree album of 18 songs in 24:49. Exclaim! heard early Minor Threat and 7 Seconds in Living Daylights and Death and Taxes.
years.xp:
Nuvo called the record genre-defining.

Wikipedia's band page dates the release to February 15, 2000; the album page says February 29.

eras.title: Back only for a good reason
eras.text: The members scattered into Paint It Black, Good Riddance and None More Black, but kept reuniting for causes. Jade Tree kept the catalog alive with a rarities disc and a documentary.

years.h: Yemin steps up to the mic in Paint It Black
years.p: He forms [[Paint It Black|90910a44-7579-4730-9499-0546159fe4e3]] in Philadelphia in 2002 as the singer, with Wagenschutz on drums until 2006.

years.cap: Reunion show at the First Unitarian Church, Philadelphia, April 2003
years.src: Wikipedia: Kid Dynamite (band) · Punknews: Kid Dynamite
years.h: A reunion for the Savio Endowment raises over $20,000
years.p: Kid Dynamite plays three Philadelphia shows for the Syrentha J. Savio Endowment, to help early breast cancer detection.

years.h: Jade Tree gathers the strays on Cheap Shots, Youth Anthems
years.p: The rarities disc (JT1085) pulls the demos, split tracks and comp tracks onto one record.

years.h: Kid Dynamite plays CBGB to help save it
years.p: The August 22 benefit for the Bowery club comes the day after Lifetime's reunion weekend ends.
years.xp: Take My Chances, Voice in the Wire and GreyArea opened. Ernie Parada came back to sing Token Entry's Birthdays.

years.h: Four Years in One Gulp puts the band on DVD
years.p: Jade Tree (JT1108) releases the documentary on February 21, 2006.

eras.title: Carry the torch, then put it down
eras.text: A 39-song tribute album showed the demand, and Kid Dynamite spent four years playing festivals from Philadelphia to Austin. In 2013 it closed the book at This Is Hardcore.

years.h: Get Outta Town Records throws a 39-song tribute
years.p: Carry the Torch has punk and hardcore bands covering the catalog.

years.cap: Jason Shevchuk at the Church, Philadelphia, September 11
years.h: Philadelphia gets the band back at This Is Hardcore
years.p: Jade Tree puts out a This Is Hardcore release on August 15, 2010; Punknews runs it as Kid Dynamite: Live from This Is Hardcore.

years.cap: Kid Dynamite at the Church, Philadelphia, September 11
years.h: A run of festivals starts at Fuck Yeah Fest in Los Angeles
years.p: Kid Dynamite plays The Fest 10 in Gainesville and FunFunFunFest in Austin to follow.

years.h: Kid Dynamite closes the book at This Is Hardcore 2013
years.p: New York shows with [[Swearin'|5b62be91-b158-40a7-a51d-43b1a3b91ec3]] and [[Joyce Manor|945d3b69-27cd-45fa-b491-52553a63dead]] follow the Philadelphia show. Punknews headlines it "for good, this time."
